title: Which takes more lives worldwide: suicide or homicide?
subtitle: Pick which takes more lives worldwide, suicide or homicide, then see the gap drawn to scale and why the news makes it feel the other way round.
form: ask choose (tap one of two drawn options)
notes: OWID: suicide 9.1 per 100,000 (WHO GHE, 2021; ~718,000 deaths) vs homicide 5.5 (UNODC, 2021): ~1.65×, not the brief’s ~2×; voice says about two-thirds more. Ghost bar ~15 per 100,000 in the early 1990s and −40% from the OWID data insight (IHME; its current rate is 9, same as WHO). 43× is from OWID 2025 (NYT, Washington Post, Fox News, US 2023 deaths) — named as three big American news outlets. After review: options mid-page, then they slide down and the bars rise from them; underline (not highlighter) on the suicide bar; bridge line before the helpline; helpline text large, upper right. During the choose reveal nothing new is drawn (engine: choose has no own reveal mark besides a stamp, which felt too playful here); the right line is kept short. Thumbnail 1 is a question card instead of the tilted band.
